prompt: A tank holds a mixture of acid and water. If 5 liters of water were added to the mixture, the result would be 18 percent acid. If instead 5 liters of pure acid were added to the original mixture, the result would be 38 percent acid. What percent of the original mixture is acid?

Car P's fuel efficiency was improved from 10 kilometers per liter to 12 kilometers per liter. Car Q's fuel efficiency was also improved, to 30 kilometers per liter. On a 720-kilometer trip, the improvement saves car Q exactly as many liters of fuel as the improvement saves car P. What was car Q's fuel efficiency, in kilometers per liter, before it was improved?

A store sets the selling price of every item so that its profit on the item is 25 percent of the selling price. During a sale, the store lowers every selling price by 10 percent. During the sale, the store's profit on an item is what fraction of what the store paid for the item?

Mo is walking through a straight railway tunnel. When he is 3/8 of the way through it, he hears a train approaching the entrance he came in by. He works out that if he immediately runs back toward that entrance at his top speed, he and the train will reach the entrance at the same moment, and that if he immediately runs forward at the same top speed, he and the train will reach the far exit at the same moment. The train moves at a constant speed. The train's speed is how many times Mo's top running speed?

Ana and Ben are 18 kilometers apart on a straight trail. At the same moment they start toward each other, Ana jogging at 5 kilometers per hour and Ben walking at 4 kilometers per hour. Also at that moment, Ana's dog starts running from Ana toward Ben at 20 kilometers per hour. Each time the dog reaches one of them, it turns around at once and runs back toward the other, always at 20 kilometers per hour, until Ana and Ben meet. How many kilometers does the dog run in all?

Angle XAY measures 11 degrees. A chain of segments, all of the same length, is drawn as follows. The first segment goes from A to a point P1 on ray AX. The second goes from P1 to a point P2 on ray AY, the third from P2 to a point P3 on ray AX, and so on, with the points alternating between the two rays. Each new point must be farther from A than the previous point on the same ray (A itself counts as the starting point on ray AY). The chain stops when no new point can be placed. How many segments does the chain contain?
ABCDE is a regular pentagon. Point F lies inside the pentagon so that triangle ABF is equilateral. What is the measure, in degrees, of angle EFD?
An equilateral triangle is drawn inside a circle of radius 6 so that all three of its vertices lie on the circle. What is the area of the triangle?
Twelve points are equally spaced around a circle. A triangle is formed by choosing three of the twelve points as its vertices. How many of these triangles have three acute angles?

A circular target has a radius of 6 inches, and a circular bull's-eye with a radius of 2 inches is painted at the center of the target. A coin with a radius of 1 inch is tossed onto the target, and the center of the coin is equally likely to land at any point of the target. What is the probability that the coin lies entirely within the target and does not overlap the bull's-eye at all?

Points A, B, C and D lie on a circle in that order as you go around it. The four arcs between neighboring points measure as follows: arc AB is 50 degrees, arc BC is 60 degrees, arc CD is 90 degrees and arc DA is 160 degrees (each arc is the one that contains none of the other points). Line AB and line DC are extended past B and past C, and they meet at point P outside the circle. What is the measure, in degrees, of angle APD?
ABCD is a parallelogram, and point P lies inside it. The area of triangle PAB is 14, the area of triangle PBC is 9, and the area of triangle PCD is 22. What is the area of triangle PAC?
In hexagon ABCDEF, all six interior angles are equal. AB = 8, BC = 7, CD = 3 and FA = 6. What is the length of side DE?

ABCDEF is a regular hexagon with an area of 72 square units. Triangles ACE and BDF are drawn inside it, and together they form a six-pointed star. What is the area of the star, that is, of the region that lies inside at least one of the two triangles?

A solid block of wood measures 10 inches by 6 inches by 4 inches. Four flat cuts, each parallel to the 6-inch-by-4-inch faces, divide the block into 5 slabs, each 2 inches thick. With the slabs kept together in their original position, one more flat cut, parallel to the 10-inch-by-4-inch faces, passes through the middle of the whole block and splits every slab into two equal pieces. What is the total surface area, in square inches, of the 10 pieces?

A closed box is a cube with inside edges 4 inches long. Eight solid balls, each with a radius of 1 inch, are placed in the box, one in each corner, so that each ball touches the three walls that meet at its corner. A ninth ball is placed with its center at the exact center of the box, and it is just large enough to touch all eight of the other balls. What is the radius, in inches, of the ninth ball?

A container is shaped like a cone standing on its point: the point is at the bottom, the circular opening is at the top, and its axis is vertical. The container holds some water, which is 4 inches deep at the center. After 380 cubic inches of water are poured in, the water is 6 inches deep at the center, and none has spilled. How many cubic inches of water were in the container before the 380 cubic inches were added?
In the coordinate plane, A is the point (2, 3) and B is the point (10, 7). Point P can be any point on the x-axis. What is the least possible value of AP + PB?

In the coordinate plane, a triangle has vertices at (0, 0), (27, 0) and (0, 12). A point is called a lattice point if both of its coordinates are integers. How many lattice points lie strictly inside the triangle (not on any of its sides)?

In the coordinate plane, A is the point (0, 0), B is the point (26, 0), and C is the point (k, 12), where k is an integer. For how many values of k is triangle ABC acute, that is, are all three of its angles less than 90 degrees?

In the coordinate plane, triangle ABC has vertices A(0, 0), B(8, 0) and C(0, 6). Point O is the center of the circle that passes through A, B and C. Point I is the center of the circle that lies inside the triangle and touches all three of its sides. What is the distance between O and I?

A club has 5 members. On Monday some of the members attend a meeting, and on Tuesday some of the members attend a meeting; on either day the group that attends may be any of the members, including none of them or all of them. Every member who attends on Monday also attends on Tuesday. An attendance record lists which members attended on Monday and which members attended on Tuesday. How many different attendance records are possible?

Six friends, including Amy, Ben, Cara and Dan, line up in a row for a photograph. Amy refuses to stand next to Ben, and Cara refuses to stand next to Dan. In how many different orders can the six friends line up?
In some four-digit positive integers, the digits alternate between odd and even from left to right, such as 3816 and 2105. How many four-digit positive integers have this property?
Three fair six-sided dice, each numbered 1 through 6, are rolled. The sum of the three numbers showing is 9. Given this, what is the probability that at least one of the three dice shows a 6?

Four friends each bring a different gift to a party. The four gifts are mixed up and handed back at random, one gift to each friend, with every way of handing them back equally likely. What is the probability that no friend gets back the gift he or she brought?

A bag holds 9 marbles: 3 red, 3 blue and 3 green. Lena draws marbles from the bag one at a time, at random and without putting any back, and she stops as soon as two of the marbles she has drawn are the same color. What is the probability that Lena makes exactly 4 draws?

Three boxes hold apples. The mean mass of the apples in box P is 155 grams, in box Q is 188 grams, and in box R is 160 grams. When the apples in boxes P and Q are put together, their mean mass is 166 grams. When the apples in boxes P and R are put together, their mean mass is 158 grams. What is the mean mass, in grams, of the apples in boxes Q and R put together?

At a summer camp, every camper belongs to exactly one activity group. Each camper was asked how many campers, counting himself or herself, are in his or her own group, and every answer was correct. 35 campers answered 7, 75 campers answered 25, and 80 campers answered 40. What is the average (arithmetic mean) number of campers per group?

Group A is a collection of numbers whose mean is 12, and group B is a collection of numbers whose mean is 51. One number is moved from group B to group A. After the move, the mean of the numbers in group A is 15 and the mean of the numbers in group B is 54. How many numbers are there in groups A and B altogether?

How many different sets of three different integers, each from 1 through 22 inclusive, can be listed in some order as an arithmetic sequence? (For example, the set {4, 9, 14} is one such set, since 4, 9, 14 is an arithmetic sequence. The order in which the three numbers are listed does not matter.)

The 25 points (x, y), where x and y are each one of the integers 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4, form a square array. How many squares have all four of their vertices among these 25 points? (A square's sides do not have to be horizontal or vertical.)
How many three-digit positive integers contain at least one digit 3 and at least one digit 7? (For example, 307, 773 and 437 are counted, but 335 is not.)

Integers are to be chosen from 1 through 40, inclusive, with no integer chosen more than once. What is the least number of integers that must be chosen to be certain that two of the chosen integers have a sum that is a multiple of 8?

A five-digit number is formed by using each of the digits 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 exactly once. For how many of these numbers is the sum of the first two digits greater than the sum of the last two digits? (For example, 53412 is counted, since 5 + 3 is greater than 1 + 2.)
For all numbers a and b, the operation # is defined by a # b = ab - 8a - 8b. How many ordered pairs (a, b) of positive integers satisfy a # b = -48 ?
A function f is defined for all positive numbers, and f(xy) = f(x) + f(y) for all positive numbers x and y. If f(8) = 9 and f(12) = 10, what is the value of f(1/6) ?
For every positive integer n, the sum of the first n terms of a certain sequence is n^2 + 3n. What is the 20th term of the sequence?
What is the sum of all real numbers x for which (x^2 - 7x + 9)^(x^2 - 10x + 24) = 1 ?
The nonzero numbers x, y and z satisfy xy/(x + y) = 2, xz/(x + z) = -6 and yz/(y + z) = -3. What is the value of x + y + z ?
Let N = 2^10 x 3^10 x 5^10. How many of the positive divisors of N have exactly 18 positive divisors?

For each whole number n, let L(n) be the least common multiple of all the whole numbers from 1 through n. For example, L(1) = 1, L(2) = 2 and L(3) = 6. For how many whole numbers n from 2 to 50, inclusive, is L(n) greater than L(n - 1)?
How many pairs of positive integers (a, b) with a < b have a least common multiple of 144?

A sequence starts with 1, and each term after the first is found by adding the sum of the digits of the previous term to the previous term. The sequence begins 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 23, 28, 38, 49, 62, ... What is the remainder when the 61st term of the sequence is divided by 9?
How many of the integers 1, 2, 3, ..., 100 can be written in the form a^2 - b^2, where a and b are positive integers?

For each three-digit positive integer N, subtract the sum of the digits of N from N itself. For example, for N = 247 the result is 247 - (2 + 4 + 7) = 234. As N runs through all the three-digit positive integers from 100 to 999, how many different results are obtained?
How many three-digit positive integers are exactly 19 times the sum of their own digits? (For example, 190 is one of them, because 1 + 9 + 0 = 10 and 19 x 10 = 190.)
A positive integer N has exactly 15 digits: four 9s, three 7s, two 5s and six 2s, arranged in some order. What is the sum of the digits of 2N?
What is the greatest prime factor of 10! + 12! ? (Here n! means the product of all the whole numbers from 1 to n; for example, 4! = 1 x 2 x 3 x 4 = 24.)
For how many integers n from 2 to 100, inclusive, is n! divisible by n^2 ? (Here n! means 1 x 2 x 3 x ... x n; for example, 6! = 720, and 720 is divisible by 6^2 = 36.)
Some of the integers 1, 2, 3, ..., 30 are to be chosen so that no two of the chosen integers have a common factor greater than 1. What is the greatest number of integers that can be chosen?
When each of the numbers 251, 323 and 443 is divided by the positive integer n, the three remainders are equal. What is the greatest possible value of n?
